metadata.title: Examining a congruency-typology model of leadership for learning using two-level latent class analysis with TALIS 2018 (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2018 school-level and teacher/principal survey responses from lower secondary schools across 47 countries/economies. The abstract reports a multilevel two-level latent class analysis framework (teacher-level and principal/school-level typologies), but it does not specify whether TALIS sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in estimation. Because the paper is an OECD/TALIS analytical report rather than a fully specified ML pipeline, the manuscript excerpt does not provide the exact weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or replicate design method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Analysts using TALIS microdata should apply the official TALIS complex survey weights and replicate weights as provided by the TALIS data documentation to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper does not model cognitive achievement scores with TALIS plausible values; instead, it estimates a congruency-typology model of leadership for learning using multilevel latent class analysis based on survey items and typology membership. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the dependent constructs used in the typology model. The excerpt also does not report a missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or multiple imputation), so the missing-data handling is treated as not reported.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD/TALIS 2018 study examines whether teachers and principals are aligned in their perceptions of core components of a “leadership for learning” framework across 47 countries/economies. Using TALIS 2018 data from lower secondary schools, it estimates a two-level congruency-typology model via multilevel latent class analysis, producing a three-group teacher typology and a three-group principal typology. The model is designed to capture misalignment through cross-level interaction and to relate typology membership to school context and covariates, including teacher and principal training and experience. The abstract reports the scale of the dataset (152,635 teachers; 9,079 schools) but does not provide predictive performance metrics because the analysis is typology-based rather than supervised ML prediction. Policy relevance is framed around identifying where leadership-for-learning capacity-building may need to be targeted differently across national contexts.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided text is an abstract and table-of-contents excerpt and does not include the detailed methodological specifications (e.g., exact TALIS item mapping, covariate list, missing-data rules, or estimation/weighting details). Because the analysis is a multilevel latent class typology (not supervised ML prediction), there are no ML algorithms, PV handling, or model performance metrics to extract into the ML-focused finding schema. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are left empty rather than fabricated from non-visible tables/sections.
